column2: There's so much tasty food that I forgot about my diet. And that I had one.
I was only checking whether the dumplings were poisoned. Three of them. For safety.
Attention! Fireworks soon. Look at the sky and make a wish.
The sky burst into gold and red. The dragon passed between the lights, and everyone thought he was setting off the fireworks himself.
Nara Arrives
In the morning a doe quietly approached the tea house. White fur, golden antlers, and calm eyes that had seen many springs.
This is Nara. She's from the forests outside town. She's wanted to see what you do here for ages.
Welcome, Nara. We have tea, lanterns and a till that doesn't know how to be quiet.
One more employee who takes nothing without asking. Accepted.
Nara bowed and stood by the door as if she'd always been there. The lanterns flared with a slightly warmer glow.
That was a bonus era. But the spiral goes on: a new circle lies ahead.
A bar right next to the jukebox is not a coincidence, it is a strategy.
A cocktail with an umbrella? The umbrella is included. The ice is not.
The record spins, life spins. Just do not spin over the bill.
The speakers are quiet, but my legs are already trembling. That is our disco.
The bass is so strong my heart is not mine anymore. I will not give it back.
Want to dance? Put your foot on the beat. Yours, not mine.
The claw is an honest game. Only the honest hand sometimes doubts.
The plush bunny is almost mine. “Almost” is the key word.
One more coin and the monkey from the machine comes home with me.
The server hums, the lights blink. All is well. Probably.
My server is up 99.9% of the time. The other 0.1% we call “rest”.
Wi-Fi catches even where reason cannot.
A shovel is the best tool for thinking. Quiet and useful.
The flowers in the pots already tasted fame. Soon they will ask for a salary.
A small tree today, a big shade tomorrow. We have to be patient.
Launch is on me. The countdown runs and the cookies are already aboard.
The rocket is ready, the fuel is in, only the till has not approved the route.
The smoke under the nozzle is not a fire, it is atmosphere.
The wheel turns, the lanterns glow. Take a good mood with you.
Every cabin is its own dream. Sadly, no seat belts.
Blink-blink. Neon outside, warmth inside.
One rule in the gallery: look, do not touch. Touching is only for buying.
This painting is unfinished. Like all my paintings. Like me.
Every brush stroke costs more than the last. The budget is a stroke too.
The fair is buzzing, wallets are trembling. All according to plan.
My songs are priceless. Although a coin finds a price fast.
The Renaissance is when everyone suddenly became an artist. Even me.

The watch ticked and the town turned pastel again, like candy from the last century. A “Milk Bar” glows on the corner, and beside it a huge jukebox stands silent.
Welcome to my bar. I'm Pip. See the jukebox? It's silent: all the records vanished right from under the needle.
Vanished? Records don't run away on their own.
Oh, they did! Those are Vinyl Hedgehogs: they spike the records on their quills and roll away. I only sold tickets to their races.
So that's who let the hedgehogs out! Help me catch them: they roll down the street, you tap each one. Catch {0} and the records are mine again.
Deal. The counter at the top will show how many you've caught.
Let's hold a record race: whoever catches more picks the song.
Shnyr, give back the ticket money, and we'll catch the hedgehogs together.
A race? I already bet on the yellow hedgehog. He's the fastest, by the way.
The money? Well... I spent part of it on props. I'll return the rest.
I'll be by the jukebox. Catch {0} hedgehogs and you'll get my thanks, and the jukebox will play more than one song again.
Deal: we come to the jukebox with full hands. I mean, records.
(tick) The Watch here. Help Pip and things will be better. Don't, and we still leave, just without thanks.
Every record is back! The jukebox plays a whole hit parade now, not one song. Thanks, friend.
The jukebox sings and the hedgehogs don't care. Quills have good hearing.
May they travel without records. And when you return, the milkshake is on me.
The watch ticked and music poured down the street. Beams of light circle above the shop, and by two giant speakers someone is desperately turning knobs.
Hi. I'm Zina, the block's DJ. See the speakers? Silent! My mirror balls ran away right before the party.
Ran away? Balls don't run.
These do. They're Disco Armadillos: they pretended to be balls and hung under the ceiling. I only rented them out for someone else's party. They got offended and went for a walk.
Without them the dance floor is dark. Help me catch {0}: they moonwalk, one step forward and one step back. Tap them!
One step forward, one step back: the main thing is to keep the rhythm. Let's go.
Let's compete: whoever catches faster DJs first.
Shnyr, return the rental money: it will go to new lamps.
DJ? Me! Just give me two speakers and zero responsibility.
The rental money? Fine. But catch the armadillos yourselves, they're scared of me.
I'll be by the speakers. {0} balls in the bag and the street has a party again. The dance floor is on me.
We catch in rhythm: one-two-three, tap.
(tick-tock) I'm the Watch. I like it when someone keeps the beat better than I do. It's rare.
All the balls are home! The lights blink in rhythm, the bass hits the chest, and the dance floor is a fairy tale. Thanks, friend.
The dance floor sparkles and the armadillos snore in their shells. The party worked.
Go on, and I'll play a farewell set. My best one, just for you.
The watch ticked and the street filled with violet glow. “Ping-ping-ping” sounds from the arcade, and a big claw machine stands by the entrance. Empty.
I'm Max, the arcade owner. See my claw machine? All the plush toys came alive and ran away.
Came alive? Some prize.
Those are Token Hamsters. I only put a coin in each cheek so they could “pass the level”. They did. Right through the door.
They dash across the grid like in a game: left, right, up, down. Help me catch {0} and the machine is full again.
Dash across a grid? Well, we're in an arcade. Tapping.
Let's play: whoever catches more hamsters wins the game.
Shnyr, return the tokens you put in their cheeks.
I'll win, because I ran away fastest. I mean, chased them fastest.
The tokens are in the cheeks, and the cheeks are free now. Catch the hamsters and the tokens will return on their own.
I'll wait by the claw machine. Catch {0} hamsters and the toys return to their places, and you get the owner's thanks.
We catch cell by cell. One more level.
(tick) The timer's still running, the game goes on. I'm just making sure nobody cheats. Except me.
The claw machine is full, the hamsters are in the toys' arms, and the high-score table has a new entry: “YOU”.
Record saved. Now the main thing is not to lose it before the next level.
I won't. Good trip! The record will wait.
The watch ticked and an invisible network lit up over the town. A server rack hums in the corner of the street, and every indicator blinks... red.
Beep. I'm Bitik, the robot consultant. Bugs got into my server! Real green beetles with antennae: they gnaw cables and break prices.
Bugs crawling out of the server? That's not in the manual.
I “accidentally” let them out. I wanted every price to be one coin. The bugs agreed and also gnawed through the password.
They glitch: now gone, now back. Help me catch {0} before they eat the whole system. Tap them!
